paper.title: Better Algorithms for Stochastic Bandits with Adversarial Corruptions

unmapped: Adaptive adversary: corruptions on round t may depend on the player's past choices and on current/past stochastic rewards (not on the current choice)
Corruption level C = sum_t ||R~^t - R^t||_inf is a realized random variable and is unknown to the learner (agnostic)
settings.definition_quote: A stochastic reward $\rew^t_i \in [0,1]$ is drawn for each arm $i$ from its reward distribution; The adversary observes the vector $\rew^t$ and generates corrupted rewards $\wt{\rew}^t \in [0,1]^K$; The player picks $i_t \in [K]$, possibly at random, and observes the corrupted reward $\wt{\rew}^t_{i_t}$. ... $C = \sum_{t=1}^T \norm{\wt{\rew}^t - \rew^t}_\infty$.

algorithms.name: BARBAR (Bandit Algorithm with Robustness: Bad Arms get Recourse)

extra_assumptions: C is the realized corruption level; algorithm agnostic to C

source.label: thm:main
source.quote: With probability at least $1-\delta$, the regret of \cref{alg:barbar} is bounded by \[ O\Bigg(KC + \sum_{i \neq i^\star} \frac{\log{T}}{\Delta_i} \log\!\Big(\frac{K}{\delta}\log{T}\Big) \!\Bigg). \]

results.notes: Regret is pseudo-regret as defined in Section 2. Algorithm takes T and delta as parameters.

source.quote: To convert the bound of \cref{thm:main} into a bound on the expected regret of the algorithm, one can set $\delta = 1 / T$ ... Thus, the expected regret is bounded by O(K E[C] + \sum_{i \neq i^\star} \frac{1}{\Delta_i} \log^2(KT)).

results.notes: Informal corollary in text, not a numbered statement.

bound.regime: C <= T/2; holds even when C is known

extra_assumptions: two-arm instance with deterministic rewards 0 and 1

source.quote: We show an $\Omega(C)$ lower bound for the pseudo-regret of any algorithm. Consider the case of two arms with deterministic rewards $0$ and $1$, and consider an adversary that at each time step swaps the rewards of the arms with probability $1/2$. ... Thus, with constant probability the algorithm will a suffer pseudo-regret of $\Omega(C)$.

results.notes: Informal argument; stated as holding with constant probability, recorded as expectation-type lower bound.
